title: The ethics, looking back
tomorrow: a restless heart. where does Augustine say it finally rests?

cards: Comment sections run on rules: who broke which one, who should be called out. In a letter to Rome, Paul runs through the old commandments: don't commit adultery, don't kill, don't steal, don't covet.
Then he folds the whole page in half. Every one, he says, is summed up in one saying: love your neighbor as yourself. So, one question for today: what sits at the center of a good life?

teach.h: LOVE IS THE FULFILLING OF THE LAW.
teach.b: Paul's answer: “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour: therefore love is the fulfilling of the law.” Love doesn't cancel the commandments; it fills them. Not stealing is what love looks like around someone's wallet.
The virtues get the same treatment: Colossians lists kindness, humility, meekness and patience like clothes, then says, “And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.”
Charity is the King James word for love. And mercy is love when someone has failed. Jesus says: “Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.”
Now a neighbor who puts mercy near the center too.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: THE MERCIFUL SHOWN MERCY.
teach.b: In Islam, a hadith, a saying of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, recorded by al-Tirmidhi, runs like this in paraphrase: the merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; be merciful to those on earth, and the One in heaven will be merciful to you.
Shared ground: mercy given and mercy received belong together. And one honest difference.

For Christians, mercy has a face in Jesus, whom they call God's Son, and in his cross. Muslims honor Jesus as a prophet, not as God's Son, and the Qur'an calls the Prophet Muhammad a mercy to the worlds.
Two neighbors, each listening to their own teacher, both saying: be merciful.

how: Christians learn the commandments in catechism classes and Sunday school, and some churches turn to Romans 13 or the Beatitudes when they talk about everyday choices; Muslims recall the Prophet's sayings on mercy and call on God as the Most Merciful.

love fills them: love worketh no ill to his neighbour.

recorded by al-Tirmidhi: be merciful to those on earth.
Christians and Muslims see Jesus the same way

games.q: a teammate cost the game with a careless foul, and the group chat is roasting him. what does 'love fulfils it' look like here?
o: the rules say he fouled, so roasting him is fair.
name the foul honestly, and give him mercy, not a pile-on.
pretend the foul never happened so nobody feels bad.
games.why: love doesn't erase the rule; it fills it. and mercy is love when someone has failed: blessed are the merciful.

practice: Choose one person likely to need mercy from you this week, someone who'll be late, wrong or sharp. Name what makes mercy hard with them, and one small plan for the moment it comes: a pause, a softer word, a second chance.
If you pray, hold their name with the beatitude: blessed are the merciful.
